caused_by.reason: Trip 1 of 2 back to the risk spike: the design left 1 fork that only a measurement can settle. O-017: unsettled design fork: Does a warm repeat of a full exe scan (SizeProbe on every file the default ProbeRule selects) net about 0 on NtfF and the WC columns from /before to /settled, as a listing-only repeat does? Its context: The design assumes yes, extrapolating the host-repeat spike's listing half (NtfF, NtxI and Ntfo 0-2 on every warm repeat). Reality has no valid answer yet: - the spike's probe half (C2 against C1) was void, and FileRepository's cold sets are used up on this boot (SC-230); - lesson #349 attributes a repeating +5 WC per walk to SizeProbe opens of reparse+sparse ICU files (unconfirmed). That would be the rule working, not failing. The losing case: per-file FCBs are torn down and re-made on each pass without a cap, so NtfF nets non-zero from churn. The F1-against-F2..F5 rule then cannot tell cache from leak on NtfF. The record's discriminator would have to change, for example by bringing back a listing-only repeat arm, which is a new arm type in Invoke-Protocol. The question can be settled in the Sandbox on created files, or by the person's session 1. The synthesis marked this as forcing a re-synthesis: the losing answer moves a component boundary, a contract or the data model. How the fork decider would measure it: Do not build on either answer yet. This goes back to the risk spike as SC-230 and is measured in Windows Sandbox. Do not use the person's session 1 for this: that Restart happens once, and it has to run with the discriminator already fixed. WHAT TO MEASURE Run in a fresh Windows Sandbox as SYSTEM. Use the app's own Scanner.Scan with ScanOptions.Default, so SizeProbe runs on every file the default ProbeRule selects. This is the scratch console's probe mode, with its Core copy checked byte-identical to SL-099 src/FsAnalyser.Core. Run each arm in its own process. Take a mark before each arm, at exit + 60 s, and, for P2 only, also at exit + 600 s to mirror /settled. Each mark is a full SystemPoolTagInformation table read with PoolWatchNative. Compare tags case-exactly, never through @{}. Live count = (pa - pf) + (na - nf). Record these tags: - NtfF, NtxI, Ntfo, Ntff, NtxF - WCsc, WCse, WCss, WCfc, WCri, WCfn, FMwi - FMfn, File, MmSt, MmCa, FMsl, FIcs, NtFs, FSim, MmSm, Ntf0, MmRe, Ntce THE SETS (A) Created files on a fresh NTFS VHDX. Flush it, detach it and re-attach it before the first arm. Detach/re-attach is what made sets cold in the earlier spikes; a standby purge does not. Use two sizes: - A-small: 400 folders x 40 files, 46-character names. - A-large: enough files that NtfF growth sampled every 2 s during P1 visibly flattens, which shows the NTFS close-cache cap was reached. Aim for at least 200,000 files. (B) The Sandbox's own C:\Windows\System32\DriverStore\FileRepository, split into two disjoint halves by a seeded shuffle. It is cold because the Sandbox boot is fresh, and it includes system files of the reparse/sparse kind. THE SEQUENCE, PER SET I0 idle (same length as an arm plus its wait), P1 cold probe scan, P2, P3 and P4 warm probe repeats, L listing-only repeat (ProbeRule false, sizeProbeCalls 0), I1 idle. On set B, run P1 to P4 on half 1 and A1/A2 listing-only on half 2 as the control. VALIDITY GATE If any of these fails for a set, that set is void and decides nothing: - P1 raises NtfF by at least max(50, 3 x the larger idle |NtfF|); - every P arm has sizeProbeCalls of at least 90% of that set's files; - every listing arm has sizeProbeCalls 0; - the quiet-host pre-wait from the earlier spikes is applied. HOW THE RESULT DECIDES THE FORK The bound for each tag is max(idle |movement| on I0/I1 for that tag, 10% of P1's rise for that tag). YES: on every valid set, NtfF from before to exit + 60 s is within the bound on at least 2 of P2, P3 and P4. NtfF from P1/exit to P4/exit is also within the bound, so nothing accumulates. P2's exit + 600 s reading agrees. The WC leak tags stay at idle movement on every warm repeat. Then the design stands as written: - the record reads F1 against F2..F5 (F3..F5 if F1 was guard-stopped) on NtfF and the full WC leak set; - no new arm type goes into Invoke-Protocol; - the clause M6 added to the measurement-preparation slice (the listing-only repeat arm on a no-go) is dropped; - SC-230 and O-016 are discharged with this run cited. NO: on any valid set, NtfF exceeds the bound on at least 2 of the 3 warm probe repeats, or accumulates from P1/exit to P4/exit, while L (or A2) on the same set stays within it. Then the design is written again: - the record's discriminator reads NtfF only from listing-only repeats; - the measurement-preparation slice must deliver a listing-only repeat arm type in Invoke-Protocol before session 1; - probe-repeat NtfF is reported, not used to decide. WC ON SET B ONLY: if a WC leak tag rises on every warm repeat of set B and stays at 0 on set A, that is per-pass WC from system files (the lesson #349 shape). It is the rule detecting what it was built to detect. Record it as such; it does not change the discriminator. VOID: if every set is void, report SC-230 as unmeasured. The second spike lap is used before this fork is escalated. No measurement answers this fork yet. The host-repeat spike's probe half (C2 against C1) was void. Its one non-binding hint was C2 within bound on all 8 tags in run 1. The host's cold FileRepository sets are used up on that boot. The losing answer adds an arm type to Invoke-Protocol, and that arm would have to exist before the person's one-shot Restart, so neither answer can be built on now. The Sandbox can answer it unattended and cheaply. Every Sandbox launch is a fresh boot, which makes FileRepository cold again. VHDX detach/re-attach has already been shown to give cold created sets. Guest pool growth does not load the host's 0.5 GB guard. The A-large set is there because the host's 2.3M probed files will certainly exceed NTFS's count-capped close cache, and the investigation saw one-for-one eviction at that cap. A test only below the cap could not tell capped churn that nets about 0 from uncapped churn that does not. Measuring now also discharges SC-230 and O-016, which M6 already made a precondition of session 1. The cost is one spike lap (0 of 2 used) and no build scope. Guessing wrong would cost a person's true Restart. The risk spike measures these first. Write the design again with what it measured: its experiments are under what reality already said about this slice.
